titleZh: 普通人的观察，也能成为科学的一部分

cet4.title: Science Begins with Looking Closely
cet4.summary: 公民科学邀请公众按照清晰方法贡献观察记录。参与者不必通晓所有知识，但需要知道记录什么、如何记录和何时求助。

paragraphs.text: A person watching birds in a park may not think of the activity as science. Yet a careful record can become useful when it follows a clear method. A citizen science project invites members of the public to contribute observations. Participants do not need to be experts in every subject. They need to understand what to record, how to record it and when to ask for help.
paragraphs.translation: 公民科学邀请公众按照清晰方法贡献观察记录。参与者不必通晓所有知识，但需要知道记录什么、如何记录和何时求助。

paragraphs.text: Imagine a project that asks volunteers to observe the same small area each week. A single visit offers only a limited picture. Repeated observations can reveal changes that are easy to miss in everyday life. Recording the date, location and conditions helps other people understand the notes. A report that says only that there were many birds is less useful than one that explains what was actually observed.
paragraphs.translation: 对同一区域进行重复观察能发现日常容易忽视的变化。日期、位置和条件等背景信息，使记录比笼统的描述更有价值。

paragraphs.text: Mistakes are a normal challenge. Two similar species can be difficult to distinguish. A photograph may help an experienced person check a record, but it may not provide a definite answer. Good projects allow participants to express uncertainty instead of forcing them to guess. Clear instructions and feedback can improve both the information collected and the experience of the people who collect it.
paragraphs.translation: 物种识别可能出错，照片与专家核查也未必消除不确定性。好的项目允许表达不确定，指导和反馈能改善资料及参与体验。

paragraphs.text: Taking part may also change how volunteers see familiar places. A tree outside a home becomes something to observe through the seasons. A quiet walk becomes a chance to ask questions. Public participation does not replace professional research. It can support it while giving people a closer connection to the process of finding evidence. The most useful contribution often begins with a modest habit: looking carefully and recording honestly.
paragraphs.translation: 参与可能让人重新注意熟悉的地方。公众观察不能替代专业研究，但能支持研究并拉近人与证据形成过程的距离。

paragraphs.text: A new volunteer can practise with a sample record before joining a larger activity. Comparing the sample with a clear example helps explain what detail is needed. Asking questions early is more useful than quietly repeating an avoidable mistake. A project becomes more welcoming when learning its method is treated as a normal part of taking part.
paragraphs.translation: 新人可以先填写样例记录并对比标准示例，了解所需细节。尽早提问比重复可避免的错误更有价值，学习方法应被视为参与的正常部分。

questions.prompt: What makes a public observation useful for science?
options: Avoiding every form of guidance.
Pretending to be certain about every identification.
Following a clear recording method.
Using enthusiastic words without any details.
questions.explanation: 规范记录使资料能够被其他人理解与比较。

questions.prompt: Why should volunteers record dates and locations?
options: They remove the need for a research question.
These details help others interpret their observations.
They make the observations impossible to compare.
They guarantee that no mistake has occurred.
questions.explanation: 背景信息会影响资料的解释。

questions.prompt: How should a project respond to uncertain identification?
options: Allow uncertainty to be recorded and reviewed.
Require volunteers to invent a definite answer.
Delete all instructions for new participants.
Treat confidence as proof of accuracy.
questions.explanation: 诚实标明不确定，比强迫猜测更可靠。

options: A guarantee that every photograph is clear.
An excuse to ignore the project method.
Proof that expertise is never needed.
A better understanding of their contributions.
questions.explanation: 反馈帮助理解如何记录以及资料如何使用。

questions.prompt: What is the relationship between citizen science and professional research?
options: Every volunteer replaces a whole laboratory.
The two must never share information.
Public contributions can support professional work.
Public participation makes analysis unnecessary.
questions.explanation: 公众参与可以支持专业研究，但不替代专业判断。

cet6.title: Citizen Science and the Value of Careful Observation
cet6.summary: 公民科学邀请公众按照清晰方法贡献观察记录。参与者不必通晓所有知识，但需要知道记录什么、如何记录和何时求助。

paragraphs.text: Science is often associated with specialised laboratories and advanced equipment, but systematic observation can also take place in familiar public spaces. Citizen science creates opportunities for volunteers to contribute records to a shared investigation. Its value does not depend on treating every participant as a professional researcher. Instead, it relies on matching an accessible task with a clear purpose and establishing procedures that make observations understandable beyond the person who collected them.
paragraphs.translation: 公民科学把公众可完成的观察任务与研究目标联系起来。价值不在于把所有志愿者变成专家，而在于建立可理解、可共享的记录程序。

paragraphs.text: Repeated observations illustrate this principle. An isolated report offers information about one moment, while records gathered consistently from the same area may help reveal patterns over time. Their usefulness depends on context: the date, location, duration and relevant conditions all affect how an observation can be interpreted. A description such as many birds may communicate enthusiasm but provide little basis for comparison. Standardised recording makes contributions more comparable without pretending that all differences in experience or circumstances can be removed.
paragraphs.translation: 重复记录可帮助识别时间上的规律，但价值取决于日期、位置、时长和条件。标准化记录能提高可比性，同时承认条件差异。

paragraphs.text: Uncertainty is therefore a feature to manage rather than conceal. Participants may confuse similar species, overlook an observation or encounter conditions that make identification difficult. Photographs and expert review can help, but they do not guarantee certainty. A well-designed project makes it acceptable to leave a record unconfirmed. Encouraging volunteers to express the limits of their knowledge is more valuable than rewarding an appearance of precision that the evidence does not justify.
paragraphs.translation: 不确定性应得到管理，而非被掩盖。照片和专家审查也并非绝对可靠，诚实表达知识边界比虚假的精确更有价值。

paragraphs.text: Feedback is important for maintaining participation as well as improving quality. Volunteers who understand how their records are checked and used can make more informed contributions. They may also recognise why an apparently uninteresting observation still matters. Conversely, collecting information without explaining its purpose risks turning participants into a temporary source of unpaid labour. A collaborative approach acknowledges their effort and creates opportunities for learning, questions and appropriate recognition.
paragraphs.translation: 反馈既改善资料质量，也维持参与。解释记录如何使用、承认志愿者努力并提供学习机会，才能形成真正的合作。

paragraphs.text: Citizen science cannot eliminate the need for professional expertise, careful analysis or a suitable research design. Nor does a large quantity of records automatically produce a reliable conclusion. Nevertheless, public participation can connect everyday experience with the practices through which evidence is assembled. People may begin to notice seasonal changes, question familiar assumptions and understand why uncertainty accompanies investigation. The achievement is both informational and educational: useful observations can accumulate while the process of science becomes more visible and accessible.
paragraphs.translation: 大量记录不会自动形成可靠结论，专业分析与研究设计仍然必要。公众参与能让证据积累过程更可见，兼具知识与教育价值。

paragraphs.text: An accessible introduction can make these expectations concrete. New volunteers might complete a practice record and compare it with an annotated example before contributing to a larger dataset. This creates an opportunity to discuss missing details, ambiguous descriptions and reasonable limits on identification. Treating training as a normal part of participation also reduces the pressure to appear immediately knowledgeable. A project gains more from a participant who asks a careful question than from one who confidently repeats an avoidable error.
paragraphs.translation: 用带注释的练习记录进行入门训练，能讨论缺失信息、模糊表述和识别边界，也减少立即表现专业的压力。谨慎提问比自信重复错误更有价值。
